props.title: Perfect

sections.content: **Perfect** (1985) epitomizes the aerobics-obsessed culture of the 1980s, starring John Travolta as a Rolling Stone reporter investigating health clubs as the new singles bars. The film captures a pivotal moment when fitness culture exploded into mainstream consciousness, following the success of Flashdance (1983) and Jane Fonda's workout empire. Director James Bridges, who previously directed Travolta in **Urban Cowboy** (1980), attempts to blend journalism ethics drama with the era's obsession with physical perfection, resulting in a fascinating time capsule of Reagan-era excess.

sections.content: The film's portrayal of journalism ethics feels particularly relevant today, echoing themes later explored in Broadcast News (1987) and **The Paper** (1994). Travolta's character faces the classic conflict between truth and exploitation, complicated by his romantic involvement with Curtis's character. The aerobics scenes, while dated, showcase the dawn of modern fitness culture that would later influence films like **Pumping Iron** (1977) and **Pain & Gain** (2013).

Jamie Lee Curtis delivers a standout performance as Jessie Wilson, building on her aerobics instructor persona from **Trading Places** (1983). Her character embodies the period's complex relationship with female empowerment through fitness, a theme that would later be deconstructed in films like **I, Tonya** (2017) and **Physical** (2021). sections.content: **Perfect** (1985) arrived at the peak of Hollywood's fitness obsession, alongside films like **Heavenly Bodies** (1984) and **Making the Grade** (1984). The genre combined the dance movie trend started by **Saturday Night Fever** (1977) with the emerging health club phenomenon. These films often featured elaborate workout sequences choreographed like musical numbers, setting a template that influenced later dance films like **Center Stage** (2000) and **Step Up** (2006).
